slots.name: describe
slots.doc:
What this source is and can do now; asked at every `info`, never cached by the host.

# Errors

Only a source that cannot even describe itself.

slots.name: open
slots.doc:
Opens a terminal. The host has already decided the grant: the request holds what the source needs and nothing
a peer may not ask.

# Errors

`NOT_FOUND` (the program), `BAD_VALUE` (a request the source cannot serve, as a program for a console),
`GONE` (the source is unavailable), `BUSY`.

kinds.name: bohio_terminal_session
kinds.doc: One open terminal. Every method takes `&self`: the host reads on one thread and writes on another.

slots.name: read
slots.doc:
Reads output into `dst`, waiting up to `wait_ms` for some. Answers the bytes read; `0` when none came in
time; `-1` when the terminal has ended and nothing more will come.

# Errors

`GONE` when the device went away.

slots.name: write
slots.doc:
Types `data` at the terminal. Answers the bytes taken, all of them unless the terminal has ended.

# Errors

`GONE` when the device went away.

slots.name: kill
slots.doc:
Ends the terminal's program and everything it started and closes the terminal. A console that starts no
program has nothing to end and only lets go of its attach. Answers how the program ended.

# Errors

Anything the source cannot end.

slots.name: exit
slots.doc:
How the program ended, `None` while it runs. A source with no program never ends it by itself.

# Errors

`GONE` when the device went away.

slots.name: pid
slots.doc:
The program's process id on the host, when it has one.

# Errors

Never, by default.

slots.name: resize
slots.doc:
Changes the terminal's size.

# Errors

`UNSUPPORTED` when the source has no size (it lacks `resize`).

slots.name: signal
slots.doc:
Delivers a signal by name (`interrupt`, `terminate`, `kill`, `hangup`, `quit`, `user1`, `user2`).

# Errors

`UNSUPPORTED` when the source has no program to signal (it lacks `signals`).

slots.name: describe
slots.doc:
What this source is and can do now; asked at every `info`, never cached by the host.

# Errors

Only a source that cannot even describe itself.

slots.name: open
slots.doc:
Opens a session on the desktop.

# Errors

`GONE` when there is no desktop to reach (the reason is the message).

kinds.name: bohio_desktop_session
kinds.doc:
One session on a desktop. The host calls it one call at a time, after its own checks of the grant, the display,
the region and the rates.

slots.name: state
slots.doc:
The session's state: who owns it, whether it is at the screen and locked, and its displays.

# Errors

`GONE` when there is no desktop to describe.

slots.name: frame_size
slots.doc:
The size of the frame `capture` of this display and region will write; the host sizes its buffer from it.

# Errors

`NOT_FOUND` for a display the desktop does not have, `GONE`.

slots.name: capture
slots.doc:
Writes a picture of `region` of `display` (all of it when absent) into `dst`, RGB, three bytes a pixel, rows
from the top, no padding, and answers its size. `dst` is at least what `frame_size` said.

# Errors

`GONE` when the session is not at the screen, `INTERNAL`.

slots.name: input
slots.doc:
Applies the events in order and answers how many it took.

# Errors

`GONE` when input is blocked, `UNSUPPORTED` for an event the source cannot make.

slots.name: cursor
slots.doc:
The pointer's display and position (an `InputModel` of kind `move`), when the source can tell.

# Errors

Never, by default.

slots.name: clipboard_text
slots.doc:
The clipboard's text.

# Errors

`UNSUPPORTED` when the source has no clipboard, `GONE` when it holds something that is not text.

slots.name: set_clipboard_text
slots.doc:
Replaces the clipboard's text.

# Errors

As `clipboard_text`.

slots.name: describe
slots.doc:
What this source is and can do now; `offers` lists the actions it takes ([`crate::vocab::power`]).

# Errors

Only a source that cannot even describe itself.

slots.name: state
slots.doc:
The system's power state now.

# Errors

`GONE` when the source cannot be reached.

slots.name: act
slots.doc:
Takes an action (`on`, `off`, `soft_off`, `cycle`, `reset`, `nmi`) and answers the state it left the system
in. A call may block until the action finished; the host bounds it by `[power] action_timeout`.

# Errors

`UNSUPPORTED` for an action the source does not take, `BAD_VALUE` for a word it does not know, `GONE`.

slots.name: describe
slots.doc:
What this source is and can do now; `offers` lists `status`, `insert_url`, `insert_reader` and `eject`.

# Errors

Only a source that cannot even describe itself.

slots.name: status
slots.doc:
The slots and what is inserted in each.

# Errors

`GONE` when the source cannot be reached.

slots.name: insert_url
slots.doc:
Inserts the image at `url`, which the source (a BMC) fetches itself.

# Errors

`UNSUPPORTED` when the source cannot fetch, `NOT_FOUND` for a slot it does not have, `BUSY` when the slot holds one.

slots.name: insert_reader
slots.doc:
Inserts an image the host serves: the source reads it through `reader` for as long as it is inserted.

# Errors

`UNSUPPORTED` when the source cannot read from the host.

slots.name: eject
slots.doc:
Ejects what `slot` holds.

# Errors

`NOT_FOUND` for a slot the source does not have.

kinds.name: bohio_block_reader
kinds.doc: A file the host lets a media source read: confined by the host, read-only, of a size the host reports.

slots.name: size
slots.doc:
The size in bytes.

# Errors

`INTERNAL` when the file cannot be measured.

slots.name: read_at
slots.doc:
Reads at `offset` into `dst` and answers the bytes read; fewer than `dst` only at the end.

# Errors

`INTERNAL` for an I/O failure.

slots.name: describe
slots.doc:
What this source is and can do now; asked at every `info`, never cached by the host.

# Errors

Only a source that cannot even describe itself.

slots.name: start
slots.doc:
Starts a program in a tree of its own. The host has already decided the grant.

# Errors

`NOT_FOUND` (the program or the working directory), `BAD_VALUE` (a request the source cannot serve), `GONE`
(the source is unavailable), `BUSY` (the source is running as many programs as it may).

kinds.name: bohio_exec_process
kinds.doc:
One running program. Every method takes `&self`: the host reads both outputs, writes the input and watches the
exit from threads of its own.

slots.name: read
slots.doc:
Reads `stream` ([`STDOUT`] or [`STDERR`]) into `dst`, waiting up to `wait_ms` for some. Answers the bytes
read; `0` when none came in time; `-1` when that stream has ended and nothing more will come. A source that
merges the two answers everything on [`STDOUT`] and ends [`STDERR`] at once.

# Errors

`GONE` when the source went away.

slots.name: write
slots.doc:
Writes `data` to standard input. Answers the bytes taken, all of them unless the input has been closed.

# Errors

`GONE` when the input is closed or the source went away.

slots.name: close_input
slots.doc:
Ends standard input.

# Errors

`GONE` when the source went away.

slots.name: wait
slots.doc:
How the program ended, waiting up to `wait_ms` for it; `None` while it runs.

# Errors

`GONE` when the source went away.

slots.name: kill
slots.doc:
Ends the program and everything it started, and answers how it ended. Calling it again answers the same.

# Errors

Anything the source cannot end.

slots.name: pid
slots.doc:
The program's process id where it runs, when there is one.

# Errors

Never, by default.

slots.name: signal
slots.doc:
Delivers a signal by name (`interrupt`, `terminate`, `kill`, `hangup`, `quit`, `user1`, `user2`).

# Errors

`UNSUPPORTED` when the source cannot signal (it lacks `signals`).

slots.name: describe
slots.doc:
What this source is and can do now; asked at every `info`, never cached by the host.

# Errors

Only a source that cannot even describe itself.

slots.name: open_dir
slots.doc:
Opens the directory `path` (absolute, in the source's own syntax) as the handle names below it are resolved
against.

# Errors

A [`failure`] (`not_found`, `denied`, `not_a_directory`...), or `GONE` when the source is unavailable.

slots.name: rename_across
slots.doc:
Renames `from` below the directory `from_root` to `to` below `to_root`, two directories of this source, in
one step. Only a source whose directories can share a file system (the node's own) offers it.

# Errors

A [`failure`] (`crosses_devices`, `unsupported`).

kinds.name: bohio_directory
kinds.doc:
One open directory. A `relative` name is below it, with `.` for the directory itself; a `confined` source refuses
one that leaves it.

slots.name: open_dir
slots.doc:
A handle for the directory `relative`.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: stat
slots.doc:
The attributes of `relative`; a symbolic link is followed only when `follow`.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: read_dir
slots.doc:
Starts listing the directory `relative`.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: open_file
slots.doc:
Opens the file `relative` as `options` say.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: create_dir
slots.doc:
Makes the directory `relative`, with `mode` where the system has modes. With `parents` the missing
directories above it are made too and one that exists is not a failure.

# Errors

A [`failure`] (`exists`, `not_found` for a missing parent).

slots.name: remove_dir
slots.doc:
Removes the empty directory `relative`.

# Errors

A [`failure`] (`not_empty`).

slots.name: remove_dir_all
slots.doc:
Removes the directory `relative` and everything in it, without following a link.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: remove_file
slots.doc:
Removes the file or symbolic link `relative`.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: rename
slots.doc:
Renames `from` to `to`, both below this directory. With `overwrite` an existing `to` is replaced in one
step; without it an existing `to` is `exists`.

# Errors

A [`failure`] (`exists`; `unsupported` when `overwrite` cannot be done in one step and the source lacks
`atomic_replace`).

slots.name: hard_link
slots.doc:
Makes `to` another name of the file `from`.

# Errors

A [`failure`] (`unsupported` for a source that lacks `hard_link`).

slots.name: symlink
slots.doc:
Makes the symbolic link `link` to `target` (text, as the link holds it); `to_directory` says a Windows link
is to a directory.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: read_link
slots.doc:
The text of the symbolic link `relative`.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: set_times
slots.doc:
Sets the times of `relative`; an absent one is left alone.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: set_mode
slots.doc:
Sets the permission bits of `relative`.

# Errors

A [`failure`] (`unsupported` where the system has no modes).

slots.name: set_readonly
slots.doc:
Sets or clears the read-only attribute of `relative`.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: statvfs
slots.doc:
The space of the file system `relative` is on.

# Errors

`UNSUPPORTED` when the source cannot tell (it lacks `statvfs`).

slots.name: next
slots.doc:
The next entries, at most `max` of them, in no order. An empty answer is the end.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

kinds.name: bohio_file
kinds.doc: An open file. Reads and writes carry their offset, so one handle serves threads that read different places.

slots.name: read_at
slots.doc:
Reads at `offset` into `dst` and answers the bytes read; fewer than `dst` only at the end, `0` at it.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: write_at
slots.doc:
Writes `data` at `offset` and answers the bytes written, all of them unless the file system is full.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: set_len
slots.doc:
Sets the file's length, cutting it or extending it with zeros.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: sync
slots.doc:
Waits until what was written is on the medium, when the source can say so.

# Errors

A [`failure`]; `unsupported` for a source that lacks `sync`.

slots.name: stat
slots.doc:
The file's attributes.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: set_modified
slots.doc:
Sets the file's modification time.

# Errors

A [`failure`].

slots.name: set_mode
slots.doc:
Sets the file's permission bits.

# Errors

A [`failure`] (`unsupported` where the system has no modes).

offers.description: What this source can do, in its kind's vocabulary ([`crate::vocab`]).

lacks.description: What this source cannot do, in the kind's vocabulary: the limits a peer should know before it asks.

available.description: Whether the source can be used now.

reason.description: Why it cannot, when `available` is false.

kind.description: A shell kind (`"sh"`, `"bash"`, `"powershell"`, `"cmd"`...) the source finds itself; empty when `argv` names the program.

listed.description: The grant lists programs: the program is the one found at that name on `path`, never what the request's environment would find.

kind.description: A shell kind (`"sh"`, `"bash"`, `"powershell"`, `"cmd"`...) the source finds itself; empty when `argv` names the program.

listed.description: The grant lists programs: the program is the one found at that name on `path`, never what the request's environment would find.

program.description: The program to start. A console source starts none and refuses a request that names one.

value.description: Its new value; absent removes it.

env.description: Changes to the environment, in order.

path.description: The host's own `PATH`, where a program without a directory is looked for.

on_host_death.description: What happens to the program's tree if the host dies without ending it: `kill`, `term` or `leave`. Absent is `kill`.

code.description: The exit code, when the source knows one.

signal.description: The signal number that ended it, when one did.

ended.description: Delivering it meant ending the program.

message.description: Something a person should know: why it was not delivered, or what was done instead.

primary.description: The display a request without a display means.

x.description: Its left edge in the desktop's layout.

user.description: The account that owns the session, when known.

active.description: Whether the session is the one at the screen.

locked.description: Whether the screen is locked; absent when the source cannot tell.

primary.description: The display a request without a display means.

x.description: Its left edge in the desktop's layout.

display.description: The display coordinates are on; the primary one when absent.

x.description: Pixels from the display's left edge.

y.description: Pixels from the display's top edge.

key.description: A key name or one character.

done.description: The state is the one the action asked for; false while a transition is still under way.

image.description: What is inserted, for a person; never a URL's query.

size.description: Size of the inserted image in bytes, when known.

argv.description: The program and its arguments, never run through a shell. Empty when `script` is set.

shell.description: A shell kind (`sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `powershell`, `pwsh`, `cmd`) that runs `script`; the source finds the shell.

cwd.description: The working directory, in the source's own syntax.

value.description: Its new value; absent removes it.

env.description: Changes to the environment, in order.

stdin.description: Whether standard input is a pipe; otherwise it is empty.

path.description: The host's own `PATH`, where a listed program is looked for.

listed.description: The grant lists programs: `argv[0]` is the one found at that name on `path`, never what the request's environment would find.

on_host_death.description: What happens to the program's tree if the host dies without ending it: `kill`, `term` or `leave`. Absent is `kill`.

reset_signals.description: Whether the program starts with SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGHUP at their default action instead of what the host inherited (Unix; a host started with `&` or `nohup` has them ignored, and its programs would never see an `interrupt`). Absent is `true`.

device.description: The device the file is on.

owner.description: The account that owns the file, as the system numbers it (a user id on Unix); absent where the system has none.

device.description: The device the file is on.

owner.description: The account that owns the file, as the system numbers it (a user id on Unix); absent where the system has none.

stat.description: What the entry is (a link is not followed), when the listing carried it; absent, the host asks.

unnamed.description: The name is not text: `name` is a lossy rendering the host cannot use to reach the entry, and it skips it.

create.description: Make the file when it is not there.

create_new.description: Make the file and fail with `exists` when it is there.

append.description: Every write goes to the end of the file, whatever offset it names.

mode.description: Permission bits of a file made, where the system has them.

blocks_avail.description: Free blocks for an unprivileged account.

files.description: Files the system can hold, when it counts them.
